screen_plans.name: Reporting Setup Page
screen_plans.purpose: The module's front door. A person finds a report of a given type, sees whether it is active and healthy, and starts a new one.

required_elements.element: Report Type Tab Set (system / my reports / shared)
required_elements.content_source: Report definitions grouped by type, scoped to the client account

required_elements.element: Per-tab report list
required_elements.content_source: Report definitions of the selected type

required_elements.element: Count Badge on each tab
required_elements.content_source: Count of reports in that type

required_elements.element: Column Chooser
required_elements.content_source: Available report columns

required_elements.element: Filter Control
required_elements.content_source: Filterable report fields

required_elements.element: Search Field
required_elements.content_source: Report name and description

required_elements.element: Pager
required_elements.content_source: Total report count for the tab

required_elements.element: Page Size Selector
required_elements.content_source: Fixed page-size options

required_elements.element: Result Counter ("showing X of Y")
required_elements.content_source: Rendered count and total count

required_elements.element: System tab always populated (never empty)
required_elements.content_source: Sand-shipped system reports

required_elements.element: Empty state with create affordance (privilege-gated)
required_elements.content_source: Zero reports in the selected tab

required_elements.element: Loading state — tabs and badges resolve before the list
required_elements.content_source: Pending report list request

required_elements.element: System tab absent without the see-system-reports privilege
required_elements.content_source: Privilege set of the signed-in person. A Technician holds see-system-reports (read-only), decided at gate 1

required_elements.element: List error state with retry, tabs still usable
required_elements.content_source: Failed report list request

required_elements.element: Per-row "source unavailable" marker
required_elements.content_source: Source dashboard resolution result per report

required_elements.element: Report Status Indicator (active / inactive / inactive-with-reason)
required_elements.content_source: Report active flag and inactivation reason

required_elements.element: Hidden-not-disabled treatment for every privilege-gated control, with no gap left in the layout
required_elements.content_source: Privilege set of the signed-in person

required_elements.element: Privilege-bound control rendering (seven named privileges, never role names)
required_elements.content_source: Admin Module privilege assignments

required_elements.element: Existing manual report creation path, unchanged and reachable alongside the new one
required_elements.content_source: The shipped SandGen manual reporting path

required_elements.element: WCAG 2.2 AA conformance across this and the other three screen surfaces — contrast, focus order, and the screen-reader consequence of hidden-not-disabled controls
required_elements.content_source: Accessibility bar decided at gate 1 (Mohamed Moanes, 2026-09-14); the produced PDF and delivery email are out of scope

user_flows: Open reporting setup page → pick a type tab → see that type's report list → click a report → open the Report Editor
Open a tab with no reports → use the empty-state affordance to create one
Owner/Admin: shared tab → open a report somebody else created → switch it off
screen_plans.notes: Three of the four states here are specified by ANNEX §B rather than by the main PRD. REQ-13 and REQ-39 are the same hidden-not-disabled rule at two scopes — the whole tab, and any single control — and both are checked at the interface rung by Check 10.

screen_plans.name: Report Editor
screen_plans.purpose: Define a report: its source, what it covers, the period, the output format, the schedule, who receives it, and whether it is on.

required_elements.element: Report Name Field (required, unique within type and account)
required_elements.content_source: Person's input; uniqueness checked against the client account

required_elements.element: Report Description Field (optional, free text)
required_elements.content_source: Person's input

required_elements.element: Source Dashboard Picker — exactly one saved dashboard
required_elements.content_source: Saved dashboards visible to the person: system default and customer-built

required_elements.element: Source-first gating — the picker is the only control until a source is chosen
required_elements.content_source: Whether a source dashboard is selected

required_elements.element: Source dashboard name displayed in the editor
required_elements.content_source: Selected source dashboard

required_elements.element: Coverage Kind Selector — sites / devices / whole portfolio
required_elements.content_source: Coverage kinds permitted by the source dashboard

required_elements.element: Coverage Scope Picker, offering only what the source dashboard permits and re-resolving when the source changes
required_elements.content_source: Polymorphic scope hierarchy, constrained by the source dashboard and the authority's access

required_elements.element: Portfolio option shown only where the source expresses portfolio scope
required_elements.content_source: Source dashboard's scope expression

required_elements.element: Coverage options visibly pending while they load
required_elements.content_source: Pending scope resolution for the chosen source

required_elements.element: Period Field, defaulted from the source dashboard and overridable
required_elements.content_source: Source dashboard's saved default period

required_elements.element: Output Format Selector — PDF or Excel
required_elements.content_source: Registered renderers

required_elements.element: PDF Content Choice — diagrams and tables / diagrams only / tables only, present only under PDF
required_elements.content_source: Fixed set of three content choices

required_elements.element: Schedule Kind Selector — repeating or one-time
required_elements.content_source: Person's input

required_elements.element: Start Date Field (required for repeating; states the last-day-of-month rule for monthly schedules)
required_elements.content_source: Person's input. Where the chosen day does not exist in a later month, the control states that the run falls on that month's last day (gate 1 round 3).

required_elements.element: Time of Day Field (required for repeating)
required_elements.content_source: Person's input

required_elements.element: Time Zone Selector, declared and shown on screen, never implicit
required_elements.content_source: Time zone list; never inferred from the browser silently

required_elements.element: Repeat Interval Selector — daily / weekly / monthly
required_elements.content_source: Fixed set of three intervals, decided at gate 1. A monthly schedule whose start day is missing from a month runs on that month's last day and never skips (gate 1 round 3).

required_elements.element: Recipient List — a scrolling list of rows, one address per row
required_elements.content_source: Person's input

required_elements.element: Address accepted without requiring a platform account
required_elements.content_source: Free-text email address, not a user picker

required_elements.element: Inside/Outside Organization Marker per recipient, derived from the address
required_elements.content_source: Address domain compared with the client's own domain

required_elements.element: Outside-organization add affordance, gated on its privilege and absent without it
required_elements.content_source: "Send outside the organization" privilege — Owner and Admin only (decided at gate 1)

required_elements.element: Active Switch, off by default on creation
required_elements.content_source: Report active flag

required_elements.element: Generate Once action — one file, one delivery, not deduplicated
required_elements.content_source: On-demand run request

required_elements.element: Save failure keeps every entered value
required_elements.content_source: Failed save response

required_elements.element: Partly-resolvable coverage shows what resolved and names what did not
required_elements.content_source: Per-scope resolution results

required_elements.element: Delete-source confirmation naming every dependent report and how many
required_elements.content_source: Reports whose source is the dashboard being deleted

user_flows: Pick a source dashboard → coverage options load → choose sites, devices or whole portfolio → choose PDF or Excel and its content → set day, time and time zone → enter addresses → switch Active on
Define a report → Generate once → exactly one file and one delivery
Arrive from a dashboard with the source already chosen
screen_plans.notes: The PRD names REQ-22 the hardest interaction in the module: the coverage picker must offer only what the source permits, and it changes when the source changes. REQ-32's option set is genuinely unspecified — it is open decision 5 and blocks this control's design. Decided at gate 1: the schedule is set inside this editor rather than in a separate step, so the five schedule controls stay on this frame.

screen_plans.name: Run History
screen_plans.purpose: Answer, per report, whether last night's run happened, what it covered, who got it, and why it failed if it did.

required_elements.element: Run row — ran-at, coverage as run, file reference, recipients as sent, outcome
required_elements.content_source: Run records, written before sending

required_elements.element: Newest-first ordering with paging
required_elements.content_source: Run records ordered by start time

required_elements.element: Never-run empty state, stated plainly and not as an error
required_elements.content_source: Zero run records for the report

required_elements.element: History absent without the read-run-history privilege
required_elements.content_source: Privilege set of the signed-in person

required_elements.element: History load failure does not block the report itself
required_elements.content_source: Failed run-history request

required_elements.element: Mid-flight run shown as running, not failed
required_elements.content_source: Run record with no finish time

required_elements.element: Failure reason on a failed run
required_elements.content_source: Recorded failure reason

required_elements.element: Inactive-after-bounded-retries state, with the creator notified
required_elements.content_source: Attempt number and report active flag

required_elements.element: Delivered-with-failures row naming the bounced addresses
required_elements.content_source: Per-recipient delivery outcome

required_elements.element: Authority-lost notice — report inactive with its reason, never silently trimmed
required_elements.content_source: Declared authority's access at dispatch

required_elements.element: Attachment-ceiling failure row — failed before sending, reason stated, file retained with no UI retrieval affordance
required_elements.content_source: Generated file size against the ceiling. The ceiling figure is still unsupplied, no editor-side guidance is shown, and retrieval is a support action rather than a self-service affordance (gate 1 rounds 1 and 3).

required_elements.element: Suppressed-run row — a run that produced no delivery is recorded as suppressed with its reason, never as a success
required_elements.content_source: Run outcome: succeeded / failed with reason / suppressed with reason

user_flows: Open a report → open Run History → see runs newest first → click a failed run → read the reason it did not send
screen_plans.notes: Decided at gate 1: run history is per report, reached from a report and scoped to it — there is no module-wide history view in this release. A Technician holds the read-run-history privilege.

screen_plans.name: Dashboard Entry Point
screen_plans.purpose: Let a person start a report from the dashboard they are already looking at, without re-picking it.

required_elements.element: "Make a report from this" action on a dashboard
required_elements.content_source: The dashboard currently open

required_elements.element: Action hidden without the create privilege
required_elements.content_source: Privilege set of the signed-in person

required_elements.element: Error fallback to the setup page with the source pre-chosen
required_elements.content_source: Failed inline-entry request

user_flows: Open a dashboard → Make a report from this → land in the Report Editor with that dashboard already chosen
screen_plans.notes: Decided at gate 1: this opens the full report editor with the source pre-chosen, not a short form — consistent with the ANNEX's specified error fallback.

required_elements.content_source: Authority resolved at dispatch, recorded on the run

required_elements.element: Quantities scaled from base unit with the label derived from the value
required_elements.content_source: Measure values in their stored base unit

required_elements.element: Panel layout reproducing the source dashboard's ordering and grouping, legible and uncut
required_elements.content_source: Source dashboard's document-canvas-element chain

required_elements.element: Content honouring the chosen variant only — no tables in a diagrams-only file, no charts in a tables-only file
required_elements.content_source: PDF content choice on the report definition

required_elements.element: Source dashboard named in the file
required_elements.content_source: Report definition's source dashboard

required_elements.element: No-readings statement instead of an empty page
required_elements.content_source: Period with no readings

required_elements.element: Named placeholder for a panel that could not render
required_elements.content_source: Per-panel render outcome

user_flows: Recipient opens the attachment → agrees it is the dashboard it came from (the module's one operator-confirm check)
screen_plans.notes: Loading and forbidden are N/A for a produced file — the ANNEX state matrix marks them so. REQ-60 is Check 23, the only acceptance check in the whole PRD that a machine cannot perform.

screen_plans.name: Generated Excel Workbook
screen_plans.purpose: The other artefact: the numbers behind the dashboard, one sheet per panel.

required_elements.element: Quantities scaled from base unit with the label derived from the value
required_elements.content_source: Measure values in their stored base unit

required_elements.element: One sheet per dashboard panel
required_elements.content_source: Source dashboard's panels

required_elements.element: Series values behind a diagram panel, not a picture of the chart
required_elements.content_source: Resolved series for each chart panel — confirmed at gate 1 (Mohamed Moanes, 2026-09-14)

required_elements.element: No-readings sheet instead of an empty sheet
required_elements.content_source: Period with no readings

required_elements.element: Sheet naming the problem for an unresolvable panel
required_elements.content_source: Per-panel resolution outcome

user_flows: Recipient opens the workbook → works with the numbers behind the charts
screen_plans.notes: The PRD calls the PDF/Excel asymmetry the most useful thing its research turned up. REQ-66 was confirmed at gate 1: a diagram panel contributes its series values.

screen_plans.name: Delivery Email
screen_plans.purpose: What arrives in the inbox of somebody who may have no Sand account at all.

required_elements.element: Subject and body identifying the report, its source, period and coverage
required_elements.content_source: Report definition and the run's resolved coverage and period

required_elements.element: No partial email on a failed run — nothing goes out and the run records why
required_elements.content_source: Run outcome before dispatch

user_flows: Scheduled run fires → email with the attachment arrives → recipient with no platform account can tell what it is
screen_plans.notes: The PRD insists this is a design surface and not a default wrapper, then specifies none of its wording. Subject line, body copy and sender identity are listed in design_requirements.md §8 under 'Needs a human in the editor'. Empty, loading, forbidden and partial-data are N/A per the ANNEX state matrix.

primary_flows: Find a report: setup page → type tab → report list → open the report
Define and schedule: source dashboard → coverage → format and content → schedule and time zone → recipients → Active on
Generate once: define → Generate once → one file, one delivery
Diagnose: report → run history → failed run → reason
Start from a dashboard: dashboard → make a report from this → editor with the source pre-chosen
Receive: scheduled run → delivery email → attached PDF or Excel
critical_paths: Source dashboard → coverage constrained by that source → produced file whose numbers match the dashboard for the same coverage and period (REQ-18, REQ-22, REQ-60)
Schedule in a declared time zone → run fires once per period → run recorded before sending → email delivered (REQ-31, REQ-42, REQ-69)
A run that cannot deliver → recorded as failed or suppressed with a reason → creator told → report inactive after bounded retries, never silently forever (REQ-48, REQ-49, REQ-72)
Privilege absent → control absent, not disabled, with no gap in the layout (REQ-13, REQ-39, REQ-73)
Source dashboard deleted or authority loses access → dependents named first, then inactive with a reason, and no file sent (REQ-54, REQ-55, REQ-56)

requirements_not_mapped_to_any_element.requirement: Report definitions, generated files and run history are scoped to one client account and unreadable from another by any route.
requirements_not_mapped_to_any_element.why: A tenancy guarantee with no UI surface of its own — it is structural separation inherited from the Admin Module, verified at the API rung by Check 14. It constrains the content_source of every list and row above rather than adding an element. Deliberately unmapped, not overlooked.
